brief.headline: Aluminium was the only base metal to fall on the 24-August board, and it fell on a day the dollar strengthened and the other four rose anyway - the first genuinely aluminium-specific signal in a week, arriving alongside a warrant line frozen for a sixth straight session and a contango that widened again to $19.50.
bullets: THE BOARD FINALLY ROLLED, AND IT ROLLED AGAINST ALUMINIUM ALONE. The 24-August official put cash at $3,215.50, down $11.50, and the three-month at $3,235.00, down $9.00. On the same board copper, nickel, zinc and lead all settled higher. Last week's rally was carried here with an explicit warning that it was a dollar event rather than an aluminium bid; this session is the controlled experiment, because the dollar moved the OTHER way - the euro fixing fell to 1.16670 from 1.17010 - and four of five metals rose through it while aluminium did not.

THE WAREHOUSE LINE HAS STOPPED BEING A PAUSE AND BECOME A REGIME. LME warrant stock printed exactly 246,925 tonnes for the sixth consecutive session, change of zero. This is not a reporting artefact: on the same board copper warrants rose 1,675 tonnes, zinc rose 125 and lead fell 1,050. Other warehouses moved; this one did not. Six identical readings say that at this price nobody will deliver metal out and nobody will draw it in.

THE CURVE AGREED WITH THE PRICE FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FIVE SESSIONS, AND THAT IS THE CLEANEST SIGNAL ON THE PAGE. The contango widened to $19.50 from $17.00 - cash below three-month, meaning no premium for prompt metal - a fifth straight session of loosening against a July average that was a $7.05 backwardation. Last week a rising price sat awkwardly beside a loosening front end; this session both softened together. Mixed signals have resolved, and they resolved toward looseness.

THE ONE CLEAN COUNTERWEIGHT IS CHINESE, AND IT IS REAL BUT NARROW. Reported ingot inventory in China's major consumption areas fell to 860,000 tonnes on Monday, down 15,000 tonnes on the Thursday and 26,000 tonnes on the Monday, so the destock accelerated. The same report says expected pre-peak-season stockpiling failed to materialise, downstream operating rates remain under pressure, and export demand is expected to weaken as the Shanghai-London price ratio recovers. WHAT TO WATCH: today's 13:20 London stock report for a seventh zero; then Jackson Hole on 27-29 August, where a new Fed chair speaks for the first time and the dollar leg gets its real test.

drivers.text: MJP Q3 settled at a roughly decade high while Asian spot drifts - benchmark and spot have decoupled, and Q4 negotiations open in about a week — The Japanese Q3-2026 quarterly benchmark settled at $395/t CIF Japan, the fourth consecutive quarterly rise from the Q4-2025 low of $86/t. The CIF Japan spot row on this board is carried at $370/t, BELOW the quarterly settlement, which is the tell: quarterly benchmarks are negotiated against expectations formed a quarter earlier, and Asian spot is now pricing a softer physical market than those negotiations assumed. Q4-2026 negotiations conventionally open in early September - roughly a week from this compile - and the pending quarter is carried here as a scenario range of $305-395/t with a NULL value because no settlement exists.
drivers.source: S&P Global Platts - Japanese Q3-2026 aluminium premium settles higher at $395/t CIF Japan

drivers.text: Roughly 77% of the US duty-paid premium is tariff, not scarcity - and the expansion leg is now confirmed in the Federal Register with a 27-August deadline — At the 50% Section 232 rate on wholly-aluminium articles, the tariff leg on today's $3,215.50 cash price is about $1,607.75/t inside a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t. THE MATERIAL CHANGE THIS RUN IS EVIDENTIAL RATHER THAN NUMERIC: what this board has been carrying as a REPORTED BIS proposal is now verified against the primary source. The Federal Register notice published 06-August-2026 requests public comment on applying Section 232 duties to fourteen additional aluminium, steel and copper derivative articles, aluminium powder among them, with comments due 27-August-2026. Scope expansion pulls more downstream product inside the tariff wall even if headline rates never change. The opposing Canadian relief leg was re-verified with a negative result for a fourth consecutive compile - no proclamation, no notice.
drivers.source: Federal Register - Request for Public Comments on the Proposed Implementation of Duties on Additional Aluminum, Steel, and Copper Derivative Articles Under Section 232 (06-Aug-2026; comments due 27-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: The Asian physical signal softened again on 24-August, and this time the softness is in the export channel rather than the inventory line — SMM's 24-August daily reports that the traditional off-season is nearing its end but that expected pre-peak-season stockpiling FAILED TO MATERIALISE, with downstream processing operating rates under pressure. Its explicit forward statement is the one that matters for regional premiums: with the SHFE/LME price ratio RECOVERED and orders on hand being digested, semis EXPORT demand is expected to weaken gradually. This is two-sided and both sides are stated: less Chinese semis competition eventually supports Western duty-paid and duty-unpaid premiums, but a softer Asian physical market pressures MJP spot into the Q4 negotiation window. The counterweight in the same report is real - ingot inventory in major consumption areas fell to 860,000 t, down 15,000 t on the Thursday and 26,000 t on the Monday.
drivers.source: AL Circle / SMM - Strait risk continues to disrupt aluminium market sentiment; peak season stockpiling falls short of expectations (24-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Freight resumed rising on 24-August and remains the quiet structural cost inside every delivered premium — The Baltic Dry Index rose 1.4% on 24-August to 2,882 points, a third consecutive gain and its highest since 12-August, with gains across all vessel segments. Capesize - the bauxite and alumina vessel class - advanced 2% to 4,643, also a third straight gain and a near two-week high; Panamax rose 1.3% to 2,131 and Supramax edged up 0.1% to 1,641. Guinea-to-China freight has been running about $35-38/t against a delivered ore price of $70-74/t, which is to say ocean freight is approaching HALF the delivered cost of the ore. Freight never appears as a line item in a regional premium quote, but it is embedded in every duty-unpaid and CIF assessment on this board, and it is currently rising rather than falling.
drivers.source: Trading Economics - Baltic Dry Index up for a third day, 24-Aug-2026 (BDI 2,882; Capesize 4,643; Panamax 2,131; Supramax 1,641)

prices.label: LME Alumina (Platts-settled exchange close)
prices.note: THE ONE CLEAN, FREE, DATED, SETTLED ALUMINA PRICE ON THIS PAGE, AND IT WAS REFRESHED THIS RUN. LME Alumina (Platts) closed $363.60/t on 21-August, UP $0.40 (+0.11%) from $363.20 on 20-August, extending an eight-session advance and taking the gain from $344.79/t on 11-August to 5.5%. This is a SETTLED exchange series rather than an assessment, which is why it carries more weight on this board than any paywalled FOB print. NO 24-AUGUST CLOSE WAS PUBLICLY RETRIEVABLE AT THE TIME OF THIS COMPILE, so the row is carried at its 21-August date rather than rolled forward silently. THE RATIO IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS AND IT REMAINS COMFORTABLE, THOUGH FRACTIONALLY LESS SO: at $363.60/t against an aluminium three-month of $3,235.00 the alumina-to-aluminium ratio is 11.24%, against a decade norm of 15-17%, so alumina is still historically cheap relative to metal and the smelter margin cushion is wide. The ratio has crept up from 11.20% as alumina firmed and metal eased - a slow, small, but consistent erosion of the cost cushion that is worth tracking rather than dismissing. Source: https://www.alcircle.com/news/lme-aluminium-cash-offer-price-rises-1-4-while-opening-stocks-remain-unchanged-at-246-925t-120885

prices.note: THE CHINESE INDEX IS DRIFTING LOWER WHILE EX-CHINA STRENGTHENS, AND THAT DIVERGENCE IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE ALUMINA READ ON THIS BOARD. SMM's Alumina Weekly Review dated 20-August-2026 marks the China index at RMB 2,681.62/mt, DOWN RMB 8.73 week-on-week, and is headlined explicitly that the spread between Chinese and overseas markets is widening. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: A MATERIALLY NEW DEVELOPMENT THIS RUN, AND IT IS A CHANGE OF REGIME TYPE RATHER THAN A CHANGE OF DEGREE. READ THAT CAREFULLY, BECAUSE ITS DIRECTION IS NOT OBVIOUS: a state that is legislating a fee schedule for transit services is a state contemplating transit, which is a step away from indefinite closure and toward a monetised chokepoint. That is BEARISH for the closure premium and BULLISH for the permanent cost of Gulf logistics - a toll, once instituted, is far harder to remove than a blockade. THE RHETORIC SIMULTANEOUSLY HARDENED, AND BOTH SIDES ARE STATED: the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council is reported saying that if the US continues economic war, no oil will pass through Hormuz or even the Persian Gulf region, following a US announcement of what was described as the toughest economic action ever imposed on any country; Iran's President is reported describing the lapsed memorandum with the US as the best achievable option and calling for the country to extricate itself from a state of 'neither war nor peace'. SMM's 24-August daily states that the ratio has RECOVERED and that, with orders on hand being digested, Chinese semis export demand is expected to weaken gradually. The arithmetic behind that sentence runs through this line: with the currency still, a recovering ratio means Shanghai is outperforming London in local terms, which erodes the arbitrage that has been pulling Chinese metal onto the export market. Chinese aluminium exports were up 18.7% year-on-year in the year to July, so anything that slows them is a genuine change in the ex-China balance - and it is one of the few clearly metal-bullish threads running through this compile.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: READ THIS RUN FROM THE TRADING ECONOMICS CROSS-ASSET BOARD ON 24-AUGUST PRINTS. The ten-year marked 4.7020%, essentially unchanged. THE LEVEL IS THE STORY RATHER THAN THE MOVE, AND IT IS COMMONLY MISREAD: a ten-year at 4.70% alongside a market pricing roughly 36% odds of a September HIKE against 64% unchanged is not a curve waiting to be cut into - it is a curve carrying live upside policy risk. FOR A COMMODITY BOARD THE TRANSMISSION IS CARRY: a high front-end rate raises the cost of financing warehoused metal, which is precisely what a widening contango has to pay for. With the cash-3M contango at $19.50 and warrant stock frozen at 246,925 tonnes for a sixth session, the market is currently paying a carry that has to clear against rates at this level - and that is one plausible reading of why the warrant line will not move. Jackson Hole on 27-29 August, with a new Fed chair's first keynote on 28-August, is the next scheduled test of this line.

headlines.title: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ON THIS BOARD AND THE FIRST ALUMINIUM-SPECIFIC SIGNAL IN A WEEK. On the 24-August LME official settlement aluminium was the ONLY one of the five base metals to fall. Cash settled $3,215.50, down $11.50 (-0.36%), and the three-month $3,235.00, down $9.00 (-0.28%). On the same board copper cash rose $53.00 to $14,344.00, nickel $80.00 to $16,940.00, zinc $5.00 to $3,985.00 and lead $5.50 to $1,862.50. WHAT MAKES THIS DIAGNOSTIC RATHER THAN TRIVIAL IS THE CURRENCY. On 21-August every base metal rose together on a falling dollar and this board carried that gain with an explicit written qualification that it was a numeraire event rather than an aluminium bid. On 24-August the dollar STRENGTHENED - the LME EUR/USD fixing fell to 1.16670 from 1.17010, the ECB fixing to 1.16640 from 1.16990 and BFIX to 1.16671 from 1.16996 - which should have pressured all five. Four rose through it. Aluminium did not. That is as close to a controlled experiment as a commodity board gets, and the result says last week's strength was borrowed from the dollar rather than earned from the metal's own balance.

SIX CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS AT EXACTLY 246,925 TONNES. THE PAUSE HAS BECOME A REGIME. LME aluminium warrant stock printed identical to the tonne on 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 24 August, with a reported change of zero on each. THE REASON THIS IS NOT A REPORTING ARTEFACT IS THE REST OF THE COMPLEX ON THE SAME BOARD: copper warrants ROSE 1,675 tonnes to 240,250, zinc rose 125 tonnes to 93,250 and lead FELL 1,050 tonnes to 415,800, while aluminium and nickel were unchanged. Other warehouses moved. This one did not. The seven-week drawdown from 337,700 tonnes on 01-June to 246,925 tonnes on 17-August has therefore ended WITHOUT converting into a build - which removes the strongest single physical argument for the summer rally while stopping short of confirming the bearish case. Six readings of precisely zero say that at this price neither warrant holders will deliver metal out nor consumers will draw it in. Warrant composition did move on 21-August, the last session publicly reported: live warrants fell to 243,950 tonnes from 244,475 while cancelled warrants rose to 2,975 tonnes from 2,450.

THE CONTANGO WIDENED FOR A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION, TO $19.50, AND THIS TIME PRICE AND STRUCTURE AGREED. Cash settled $19.50 BELOW the three-month on 24-August, widened from $17.00 on 21-August and $1.00 on 20-August, against a July average that was a $7.05 BACKWARDATION. CONVENTION STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST COMMONLY INVERTED TERM IN THIS MARKET: cash below three-month is CONTANGO, cash above three-month is BACKWARDATION. THE CHANGE WORTH NAMING IS THE INTERNAL CONSISTENCY. Last week's rally sat awkwardly beside a loosening front end - a flat price rising while the market declined to pay anything extra for metal it could have that day, which is an internal contradiction this board flagged as the rally's weakest feature. On 24-August both softened together. The mixed signal has resolved, and it resolved toward looseness. Roughly $27 of front-end swing across the month has taken the market from paying a premium for prompt metal to charging one to carry it.

THE CLEANEST BULLISH DATUM ON THIS COMPILE, AND IT IS CHINESE. SMM's report published 24-August puts aluminium ingot inventory at China's major consumption areas at 860,000 tonnes as of Monday, DOWN 15,000 tonnes from the previous Thursday and DOWN 26,000 tonnes from the previous Monday. The destocking trend not only continued but ACCELERATED against the prior week's 23,000-tonne weekly draw. SMM describes the destock explicitly as providing bottom support for aluminium prices. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS CARRIED ALONGSIDE IT RATHER THAN BURIED: the same report says expected pre-peak-season stockpiling failed to materialise and that downstream processing operating rates remain under pressure, and separate SMM statistics put Chinese BILLET inventory at a five-year seasonal high with processing fees rising. A destocking ingot line beside a building billet line is metal moving one step down the chain, which is movement rather than consumption - but the acceleration is real and it is reported as real.

THE PEAK SEASON HAS NOT SHOWN UP, AND NOW THE EXPORT CHANNEL IS EXPECTED TO CLOSE TOO. SMM's 24-August daily states that the traditional consumption off-season is nearing its end but that expectations for pre-peak-season stockpiling FAILED TO MATERIALISE, with operating rates across downstream processing sectors under pressure overall. Its forward statement is the newer and more consequential half: with the SHFE/LME price ratio RECOVERED and orders on hand being digested, semis EXPORT demand is expected to WEAKEN gradually. Chinese aluminium exports were running 18.7% higher year-on-year in the year to July, so a closing arbitrage is a genuine change in the ex-China balance - bullish for metal availability outside China over time, bearish for the read on Chinese end-demand today. On the demand side there is one narrow positive: SMM reports that US tariffs on silicon-based products have prompted a recovery in order books at some Chinese photovoltaic extrusion enterprises, though overall PV extrusion operating rates did not improve significantly.

A CHANGE OF REGIME TYPE RATHER THAN A CHANGE OF DEGREE, AND ITS DIRECTION IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. SMM's 24-August daily reports that the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission has PASSED ARTICLE 3 of a 'Strategic Action Plan for Ensuring the Safety and Development of the Strait of Hormuz', under which Iran will CHARGE FEES for maritime services, environmental services, fuel supply in special circumstances, insurance, safety and other services. A state legislating a fee schedule for transit services is a state contemplating transit - a step away from indefinite closure and toward a monetised chokepoint. That is BEARISH for the closure premium and BULLISH for the permanent cost of Gulf logistics, because a toll once instituted is far harder to remove than a blockade. THE RHETORIC HARDENED IN PARALLEL AND BOTH SIDES ARE REPORTED: the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council is reported saying no oil will pass through Hormuz or the Persian Gulf if the US continues economic war, following a US announcement described as the toughest economic action ever imposed on any country, while Iran's President is reported calling the lapsed US memorandum the best achievable option and urging the country out of a state of 'neither war nor peace'.

UPGRADED THIS RUN FROM REPORTED TO PRIMARY-SOURCED, AND THE DEADLINE IS TWO DAYS AWAY. What this board has been carrying as a reported Bureau of Industry and Security proposal is now verified against the Federal Register itself. The notice published 06-August-2026 requests public comment on implementing Section 232 duties on FOURTEEN ADDITIONAL aluminium, steel and copper derivative articles - aluminium powder, brass-wind musical instruments and parts, parts of welding machines, floor safes, certain electric conductor cables, fire extinguishers, parts of heat exchange units, parts of certain hydraulic engines and motors, certain self-propelled cranes and straddle carriers, tanker trailers and semi-trailers, self-loading agricultural trailers, certain other trailers and certain filled steel containers. COMMENTS ARE DUE BY 27-AUGUST-2026. THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS IS SCOPE VERSUS RATE: a wider derivative list pulls MORE downstream aluminium product inside the tariff wall even if headline rates never change, which is premium-SUPPORTIVE at exactly the moment the market has already priced premium-destructive Canadian relief that no legal text supports. Both are live and they push opposite ways.

FREIGHT RESUMED RISING ON 24-AUGUST AND THE VESSEL CLASS THAT MOVES BAUXITE LED IT. The Baltic Dry Index rose about 1.4% to 2,882 points, a THIRD consecutive gain and its highest since 12-August, with gains across all vessel segments. The Capesize index - the bauxite and alumina class - advanced 2.0% to 4,643, also a third straight gain and a near two-week high; Panamax rose 1.3% to 2,131 and Supramax edged up 0.1% to 1,641. The index closed 2,791 on 20-August and 2,841 on 21-August, so three sessions have retraced the prior weakness in full. Guinea-to-China freight has been running about $35-38/t against a delivered ore price of $70-74/t, meaning ocean freight is approaching HALF the delivered cost of the ore. Freight never appears as a line item in a regional premium quote but is embedded in every duty-unpaid and CIF assessment on this board. Rising Capesize into a widening contango is a delivered cost rising while the metal price falls.

THE ONE SETTLED, FREE, DATED ALUMINA PRICE ON THIS PAGE ROSE AGAIN, AND THE MARGIN CUSHION COMPRESSED FROM BOTH ENDS. LME Alumina (Platts) closed $363.60/t on 21-August, up $0.40 (+0.11%) from $363.20 on 20-August - an eighth consecutive higher close, taking the advance from $344.79/t on 11-August to 5.5%. No 24-August close was publicly retrievable at the time of this compile, so the row is carried at its 21-August date rather than rolled silently. AGAINST A THREE-MONTH ALUMINIUM PRICE OF $3,235.00 THE ALUMINA-TO-ALUMINIUM RATIO IS NOW 11.24%, against a decade norm of 15-17%. Alumina therefore remains historically cheap relative to metal and the smelter margin cushion is still wide - but it is compressing from both ends simultaneously, with alumina firming while the metal price eases. That is a slow and small erosion rather than a squeeze, and it is tracked rather than dramatised.

THE DATED MACRO EVENT IS NOW TWO DAYS AWAY AND A NEW FED CHAIR SPEAKS FIRST. The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City hosts the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium from 27 to 29 AUGUST 2026 at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming, on the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy', with roughly 120 policymakers and economists from more than 70 countries attending. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers the keynote on the morning of FRIDAY 28-AUGUST - his first Jackson Hole address in the role. THE TRANSMISSION TO THIS BOARD IS DIRECT AND ALREADY DEMONSTRATED: the 21-August rally was a dollar event and the 24-August fall was a dollar event running the other way. Rate expectations have shifted this month - CME FedWatch is reported around 24-August at roughly 36% for a September HIKE against 64% unchanged, down from about 50% for a hike earlier in the month, and gold reached a three-month high into the event. A dovish read restores the dollar weakness that did the work last week; a hawkish read removes it, and aluminium currently has very little of its own to fall back on.

CRUDE REVERSED AND GAS DID NOT, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS ITSELF THE INFORMATION. Brent fell 2.57% to $91.96 and WTI 2.54% to $84.85 on the 24-August cross-asset board, on reported positioning ahead of further US sanctions action, undoing a meaningful part of two consecutive weekly advances. European TTF gas rose 3.80% to EUR 68.37/MWh on the same board. WHEN OIL AND GAS MOVE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS THE GAS MOVE IS USUALLY REGIONAL AND PHYSICAL RATHER THAN A GLOBAL RISK REPRICING. For aluminium the two legs cut opposite ways and both are stated: crude down is the first counter-evidence against the anode-carbon re-inflation thesis, because green and calcined petroleum coke are refinery co-products; gas up pressures European smelter margins directly, since power in the marginal European hour is frequently gas-set, and this year's two largest aluminium supply headlines - a Gulf smelter shutdown and a Brazilian refinery cut to half rate - were both gas-supply events.

THE CARBON RE-INFLATION EVIDENCE STANDS, BUT ITS UPSTREAM DRIVER WOBBLED. Chinese customs data published 23-August put July-2026 prebaked anode EXPORTS at 211,700 tonnes - up 21.86% year-on-year and down 24.40% month-on-month - at an average export price of about USD 1,031.80/t, UP 12.34% month-on-month and 24.94% year-on-year, with January-July cumulative exports of 1.5183 million tonnes, up 23.47% year-on-year. Anodes are roughly 13-16% of smelter cash cost at about 0.42 tonnes per tonne of metal, so a double-digit monthly price move is material rather than marginal. It corroborates the coal tar pitch series, which rose for four consecutive weekly assessments to RMB 4,960/t. THE WOBBLE IS CRUDE: Brent fell 2.6% on 24-August after two weekly advances, and petroleum coke is a refinery co-product. THE BASIS DISTINCTION IS PRESERVED RATHER THAN BLURRED: the export price is a dollar unit value and the sparkline on this dashboard charts the Chinese domestic RMB tender, so the export figure is reported in commentary and deliberately kept off the chart. The September domestic tender around 31-August is the confirmation test.

THE BILLET LINE IS THE REASON THE INGOT DESTOCK CANNOT BE READ AS PURE CONSUMPTION. SMM statistics put Chinese aluminium BILLET inventory in major consumption areas at 143,000 tonnes as of 20-August - up 500 tonnes from the previous Monday, up 6,000 tonnes from the previous Thursday, and THE HIGHEST FOR THE SAME PERIOD IN FIVE YEARS - on a continuous buildup pace, with billet processing fees RISING even as the flat price fell. A rising conversion fee against a building stock of converted metal is the signature of a bottleneck rather than of demand. Read beside an ingot social inventory that fell 26,000 tonnes week-on-week to 860,000 tonnes, the combined picture is metal being moved one step down the chain and stopping there - a transfer, not a disappearance. Separately, China's social inventory of cast aluminium alloy ingots rose 2,500 tonnes week-on-week to 28,100 tonnes, a second consecutive weekly build with the magnitude widening.

THE SCRAP CHANNEL IS TIGHTENING FOR POLICY REASONS AS MUCH AS PRICE ONES, AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS BECAUSE SECONDARY METAL IS THE MARGINAL SUBSTITUTE FOR PRIMARY. SMM customs data put China's aluminium scrap imports at approximately 119,600 tonnes in July 2026, DOWN month-on-month from 133,000 tonnes in June, attributed to the earlier inversion of the China-versus-overseas price spread and to shipment delays that kept replenishment of high-quality overseas scrap low. TWO POLICY EFFECTS ARE COMPOUNDING IT AND BOTH ARE REPORTED: the UAE's aluminium scrap export ban and the EU's tariff increase are described as continuing to contract supply out of Europe and the Middle East, further consolidating South-East Asia as the major supplementary source. SMM's A00 spot marked RMB 23,680/t, up RMB 80, while scrap prices held broadly stable, narrowing the primary-to-scrap spread. Less imported scrap into the world's largest consumer is, at the margin, primary-supportive.

THE SUPPLY-RELIEF SCHEDULE IS UNCHANGED, DATED AND STILL THE DOMINANT STRUCTURAL FACT ON THIS BOARD, AND SMM RESTATED THE AGGREGATE ON 24-AUGUST: outside China, driven by new capacity and production resumptions, daily average production is expected to CONTINUE RECOVERING. The operational detail behind that sentence is unchanged and no new disclosure was published in the 24-25 August window, which is reported as absence rather than dressed up as progress. The Gulf smelter struck early in the conflict is running at about 18% of its 1,262 pots with hot metal guided back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 and its 2.4 Mt/y refinery to full technical capability by end-2026; the region accounted for roughly 10% of global primary production before the conflict. Australia's largest smelter, at up to 590,000 t/y, has been secured to 2038 on an A$2.5bn federal-and-state support package after being flagged for possible closure from 2029. The largest refinery outside China is back at full rate after a three-day gas outage. None of this is new today; all of it caps the recovery.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 37.6% directional hit rate against a 69.8% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.29% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (101 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-05-29). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, AND THE SEVENTH TEST OF THE SAME WAREHOUSE QUESTION. Two things print together and the second matters more. (1) THE SETTLEMENT: does 24-August's aluminium-specific weakness repeat, or was one session of underperformance against a rising complex noise? The immediate technical hurdle is the 38.2% retracement at $3,254.60, now $19.60 above the $3,235.00 forward and unrecovered since 18-August; the explicit downside invalidation is the 28-July swing low at $3,159.50, now $56.00 below cash and $20.00 nearer than on Friday. SMM's independently published core range is $3,200-$3,300/mt, which puts this settlement in the lower half of an outside forecaster's band. (2) THE STOCK REPORT, WHICH IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO AND IS A THREE-WAY TEST: (a) a SEVENTH consecutive zero confirms stasis as the settled regime and the flat line stops being news at all; (b) an outright BUILD confirms the seven-week drawdown is over and is the strongest bearish confirmation available; (c) a RESUMED DRAW would be the best evidence the bull case has had since 11-August. WATCH THE SPREAD ALONGSIDE THE PRICE: a rally that NARROWS the $19.50 contango means something entirely different from one that widens it, and the last five sessions have all widened it.

THE SECTION 232 INCLUSIONS COMMENT WINDOW CLOSES, AND IT IS NOW PRIMARY-SOURCED RATHER THAN REPORTED. The Federal Register notice published 06-August-2026 requests public comment on applying Section 232 duties to FOURTEEN additional aluminium, steel and copper derivative articles - aluminium powder and certain electric conductor cables among them - with comments due 27-AUGUST-2026 ahead of a final determination. THIS IS SCOPE, NOT RATE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: a wider derivative list pulls MORE downstream aluminium product inside the tariff wall even if headline rates never change, which is premium-SUPPORTIVE at exactly the moment the market has already priced premium-destructive Canadian relief that no legal text supports. Both are live and they push in opposite directions. Nothing goes on this board as settled law until final text exists.

JACKSON HOLE, AND FED CHAIR KEVIN WARSH'S FIRST KEYNOTE IN THE ROLE ON THE MORNING OF FRIDAY 28-AUGUST. The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City hosts the symposium at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming, on the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy', with roughly 120 policymakers and economists from more than 70 countries attending. THE TRANSMISSION TO THIS BOARD IS NO LONGER THEORETICAL - IT HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED TWICE IN THREE SESSIONS. On 21-August a falling dollar lifted every base metal together; on 24-August a rising dollar coincided with aluminium falling alone. Rate expectations moved this month: CME FedWatch is reported around 24-August at roughly 36% for a September HIKE against 64% unchanged, down from about 50% for a hike earlier in the month, and gold reached a three-month high into the event. A dovish read restores the dollar weakness that did the work last week; a hawkish read removes it. Given that aluminium's front end has loosened for five consecutive sessions and the warrant line has not moved in six, the metal currently has very little of its own to fall back on.

THE SEPTEMBER PREBAKED ANODE TENDER SETTLEMENT, AND IT NOW ARBITRATES A GENUINE DISAGREEMENT RATHER THAN MERELY CONFIRMING A TREND. The Chinese domestic tender cycle settles around month-end; the August cycle printed RMB 5,630/t, down RMB 53/t. On one side, the 23-August customs data show the July average anode EXPORT price up 12.34% month-on-month to about $1,031.80/t and coal tar pitch has risen for four consecutive weeks. On the other, Brent fell 2.6% on 24-August and petroleum coke is a refinery co-product. IF THE DOMESTIC SETTLEMENT FOLLOWS THE EXPORT PRICE HIGHER, carbon cost re-inflation is confirmed on the same basis this dashboard charts and the anode sparkline turns up. IF IT DOES NOT, the two series have decoupled and the export move was a mix or freight effect rather than a cost signal. Green petcoke 3B settlements and the coal tar pitch weekly are the corroborating series.

THE LME'S THREE NEW P1020A PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE INTENDED TO PUBLISH FOR THE FIRST TIME, INCLUDING A DUTY-UNPAID ROTTERDAM SERIES. The exchange ran a public consultation which CLOSED 19-AUGUST-2026 on launching the series, with intended first publication from 01-September-2026. THIS IS A STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT RATHER THAN A PRICE EVENT AND IT MATTERS TO THIS BOARD SPECIFICALLY: the European duty-unpaid row is currently carried at a stale public mark with its date visible, because the Fastmarkets, Argus and SMM assessments are all paywalled and nothing free and dated prints. A free, dated, exchange-published duty-unpaid series would give that row a live source for the first time. Carried as an intention, not as a certainty.

THE US-CANADA SECTION 232 PROCLAMATION, STILL THE SINGLE LARGEST UNRESOLVED POLICY ITEM ON THIS BOARD AND RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN WITH A NEGATIVE RESULT FOR A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE COMPILE. No proclamation and no Federal Register notice halving rates on Canadian aluminium could be found; the legal rate remains 50% on wholly-aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives under the April-2026 two-tier structure, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. THE PREMIUM HAS NEVERTHELESS ALREADY MOVED, falling 8.2% in one session to about 95 cents a pound with later months down more than 12%. THE TEST IS BINARY AND EITHER OUTCOME IS TRADEABLE INFORMATION: if the text is published, the remaining tariff leg of the US duty-paid premium compresses further; if weeks continue to pass without it, the 8.2% move was an expectation that will have to be given back.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open in early September - roughly a week from this compile - and settle mid-to-late in the month. Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan, the fourth consecutive quarterly rise from the Q4-2025 low of $86/t. THE PENDING QUARTER IS CARRIED HERE AS A SCENARIO RANGE OF $305-395/t WITH A NULL VALUE RATHER THAN A POINT ESTIMATE, because no settlement exists and inventing one would be fabrication. The two forces pull against each other and the balance tilted further toward the lower half this run: ex-China alumina strength, rising Capesize freight and carbon cost re-inflation argue for a hold or a rise, while a five-year-high Chinese billet stockpile, SMM's observation that peak-season stockpiling failed to materialise, and its new expectation that semis export demand will weaken as the SHFE/LME ratio recovers all argue for the lower half of the range.

THREE STANDING UNDATED ITEMS, THE FIRST OF WHICH DEVELOPED THIS RUN. FIRST AND MOST LOAD-BEARING: the Strait of Hormuz regime, where Iran's parliamentary security commission is reported to have passed an article establishing FEES for maritime, environmental, fuel-supply, insurance and safety services - a monetised chokepoint rather than a closed one, which is bearish for the closure premium and bullish for the permanent cost of the corridor. The last primary maritime source, UKMTO/JMIC Update 086 of 18-August, still sets the threat at SEVERE with cargo transits of exactly zero on three consecutive days. THIRD: the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism after the BRICS ministerial objection of 22-August. None of the three has a publishable date, which is exactly why they are listed as standing watch items rather than given false precision.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD AND RESTATED ON A FRESH SOURCE DATE THIS RUN. SMM's 24-AUGUST DAILY PUTS THE AGGREGATE PLAINLY: outside China, driven by new capacity commissioning and production resumptions, daily average production is expected to CONTINUE RECOVERING. The operational schedule beneath that sentence is unchanged and no new company disclosure appeared in the 24-25 August window, which is reported as absence rather than progress: the Gulf smelter at about 18% of 1,262 pots with hot metal guided to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 and its 2.4 Mt/y refinery to full technical capability by end-2026; the Australian smelter secured to 2038 on A$2.5bn of federal and state support covering up to 590,000 t/y after being flagged for possible closure from 2029; the largest refinery outside China back at full rate after a three-day gas outage; the Spanish smelter restart completed in April; 75,000 t/y restarting in Slovakia in Q4-2026; a US smelter at full capacity for the first time since 2015. THE FINANCIAL EVIDENCE REMAINS THE MORE TELLING HALF: a collapsed alumina price is not throttling the ex-China pipeline, it is being CONVERTED into it, with a listed producer funding a 250,000 t/y Indonesian first phase from a cash balance that more than doubled.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED AND HAS NOW BEEN STOPPED FOR SIX CONSECUTIVE PUBLISHED SESSIONS AT EXACTLY 246,925 TONNES. FULLY MATERIALISED, HARDENING, AND NO LONGER DESCRIBABLE AS A PAUSE. 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 24 August all identical to the tonne with a reported change of zero. THE DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE THIS RUN IS THAT IT IS NOT A REPORTING ARTEFACT, AND THE PROOF SITS ON THE SAME BOARD: copper warrants ROSE 1,675 tonnes to 240,250, zinc rose 125 tonnes to 93,250 and lead FELL 1,050 tonnes to 415,800, while aluminium and nickel were unchanged. Other warehouses moved; this one did not. The seven-week drawdown from 337,700 tonnes on 01-June to 246,925 tonnes on 17-August has ended WITHOUT converting into a build, which removes the single strongest physical argument for the summer rally while stopping short of confirming the bearish one. Six readings of precisely zero say that at this price neither warrant holders will deliver metal out nor consumers will draw it in - and a $19.50 contango is exactly the structure that pays both of them to stay still. TODAY'S 13:20 REPORT IS A SEVENTH TEST OF THE SAME THREE-WAY QUESTION.

THE HORMUZ REGIME MAY BE CHANGING TYPE RATHER THAN DEGREE, AND THE DIRECTION IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. THIS IS THE MOST GENUINELY NEW ITEM ON THE REGISTER THIS RUN. SMM's 24-August daily reports that Iran's parliamentary National Security and Foreign Policy Commission has PASSED ARTICLE 3 of a 'Strategic Action Plan for Ensuring the Safety and Development of the Strait of Hormuz', under which Iran will CHARGE FEES for maritime services, environmental services, fuel supply in special circumstances, insurance, safety and other services. A state legislating a transit fee schedule is a state contemplating transit. THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH ARE STATED: it is BEARISH for the closure premium currently embedded in Gulf supply expectations, and BULLISH for the permanent cost of the corridor, because a toll once instituted is far harder to remove than a blockade. THE RHETORIC HARDENED IN PARALLEL: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary is reported saying no oil will pass through Hormuz or the Persian Gulf if the US continues economic war, after a US announcement described as the toughest economic action ever imposed on any country. THE LAST PRIMARY MARITIME SOURCE IS CARRIED AT ITS OWN DATE: UKMTO/JMIC Update 086 of 18-August sets the threat at SEVERE with cargo transits of exactly zero on three consecutive days. TREND HELD AT UP - a committee passage is not an implemented tariff schedule, and escalating or de-escalating a risk on a procedural step is how a register loses its meaning.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL - AND THE EVIDENCE THIS RUN IS GENUINELY TWO-SIDED, SO THE TREND IS HELD AT UP RATHER THAN RAISED. THE BEARISH HALF, FROM SMM's 24-AUGUST DAILY: the traditional off-season is nearing its end but expectations for pre-peak-season stockpiling FAILED TO MATERIALISE, operating rates across downstream processing sectors remain under pressure, and - the newer and more consequential statement - with the SHFE/LME price ratio RECOVERED and orders on hand being digested, semis EXPORT demand is expected to WEAKEN gradually. Chinese billet inventory reached 143,000 tonnes on 20-August, the highest for the period in five years, with processing fees RISING into a falling flat price, and cast aluminium alloy social inventory built for a second consecutive week to 28,100 tonnes. THE BULLISH HALF IS REAL AND IS NOT BURIED: ingot inventory at major consumption areas fell to 860,000 tonnes, down 15,000 tonnes on the Thursday and 26,000 tonnes on the Monday - an ACCELERATING destock that SMM itself describes as bottom support for prices. THE SYNTHESIS IS THAT AN ACCELERATING INGOT DRAW BESIDE A FIVE-YEAR-HIGH BILLET STOCK IS CONVERSION RATHER THAN CONSUMPTION, which is why the risk is held rather than reduced. One narrow positive is reported: US tariffs on silicon-based products have prompted a recovery in some Chinese PV extrusion order books, though overall PV extrusion rates did not improve.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND HELD AT DOWN, AND THIS RUN SUPPLIES THE BEST EVIDENCE YET FOR HOLDING IT THERE. The 24-August session was the cleanest available test of how much of the summer advance was financial: the dollar STRENGTHENED, four of five base metals rose through it, and aluminium alone fell. That is froth being taken out rather than a crowd being caught - the give-back from the 11-August high has now run 4.67% on cash, and a long that has already been trimmed over eleven sessions is a smaller forward risk than one that has not. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS KEPT VISIBLE: the contango has widened for five consecutive sessions and the flat price is still $56.00 above the 28-July invalidation, so there is room below. Jackson Hole on 27-29 August, with a new Fed chair's first keynote on Friday morning, is where this gets its next and largest test - and on the evidence of 24-August the metal has little of its own to fall back on if the macro bid is withdrawn.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND HELD AT DOWN, BUT THE CUSHION IS COMPRESSING AND THE COMPRESSION IS REPORTED RATHER THAN IGNORED. The settled LME Alumina (Platts) contract closed $363.60/t on 21-August, an eighth consecutive higher close and up 5.5% from $344.79/t on 11-August. Against a three-month aluminium price of $3,235.00 the alumina-to-aluminium ratio is 11.24%, against a decade norm of 15-17%, so the smelter margin cushion is still wide - but it is now narrowing from BOTH ends at once, with alumina firming while metal eases. THE STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE FOR THE DOWN TREND IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS STRONG: a listed producer's audited-standard H1-2026 accounts disclose a realised alumina selling price of USD 320/t across 1.296 Mt of actual sales against USD 529/t a year earlier, with the average international price on an LME Platts basis put at about USD 307/t against about USD 447/t. A volume-weighted realised price from a seller's accounts is better evidence than any assessment. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS BEARISH FOR THE METAL AND IS STATED PLAINLY: a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THIS RUN THE THESIS LOST ONE OF ITS THREE LEGS, WHICH IS REPORTED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED. THE TWO SURVIVING LEGS: Chinese customs data published 23-August put the July average prebaked anode EXPORT price at about $1,031.80/t, up 12.34% month-on-month and 24.94% year-on-year on 211,700 tonnes of exports, and anodes are roughly 13-16% of smelter cash cost at about 0.42 tonnes per tonne of metal; coal tar pitch has risen for four consecutive weekly assessments to RMB 4,960/t. THE LEG THAT BROKE IS CRUDE: Brent fell 2.57% to $91.96 and WTI 2.54% to $84.85 on 24-August, undoing part of two consecutive weekly advances, and green and calcined petroleum coke are refinery co-products loosely tethered to the crude complex. One session is not a trend and the two Chinese series have not turned, so the trend is HELD AT UP rather than cut - but a cost thesis that leans on crude must be marked when crude moves against it. THE OPPOSING ENERGY LINE WENT THE OTHER WAY: European TTF gas rose 3.80% to EUR 68.37/MWh, which pressures European smelter margins directly. THE SEPTEMBER DOMESTIC ANODE TENDER AROUND 31-AUGUST IS THE CONFIRMATION TEST.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM - AND THE EXPANSION LEG WAS UPGRADED THIS RUN FROM REPORTED TO PRIMARY-SOURCED, WHICH IS A MATERIAL STRENGTHENING OF THIS ENTRY'S EVIDENCE BASE. THE FEDERAL REGISTER NOTICE PUBLISHED 06-AUGUST-2026 requests public comment on implementing Section 232 duties on FOURTEEN ADDITIONAL aluminium, steel and copper derivative articles - aluminium powder, brass-wind instruments and parts, parts of welding machines, floor safes, certain electric conductor cables, fire extinguishers, parts of heat exchange units, parts of certain hydraulic engines and motors, certain self-propelled cranes and straddle carriers, tanker trailers and semi-trailers, self-loading agricultural trailers, certain other trailers and certain filled steel containers - WITH COMMENTS DUE 27-AUGUST-2026, two days from this compile. THE OPPOSING RELIEF LEG RETURNED A NEGATIVE RESULT FOR A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE COMPILE: no proclamation and no Federal Register notice halving rates on Canadian aluminium exists, so the legal position remains 50% on wholly-aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15%. THE MARKET HAS PRICED THE RELIEF ANYWAY - the September Midwest premium fell 8.2% in a single session to about 95 cents a pound - so with the statute unchanged roughly 77% of the US duty-paid premium is policy rather than physical scarcity. Scope expansion and rate relief point in opposite directions and both are live. Nothing is carried here as fact until legal text exists.

FREIGHT AND DELIVERED-COST INFLATION INSIDE EVERY REGIONAL PREMIUM. RAISED TO AN EXPLICIT REGISTER ENTRY THIS RUN BECAUSE IT MOVED THREE SESSIONS RUNNING AND BECAUSE IT IS THE COST LINE MOST LIKELY TO BE OVERLOOKED - it is never quoted separately on any premium assessment. The Baltic Dry Index rose 1.4% to 2,882 on 24-August, a third consecutive gain and its highest since 12-August, with gains across all vessel segments; Capesize - the bauxite and alumina vessel class - advanced 2.0% to 4,643, also a third straight gain and a near two-week high. The index closed 2,791 on 20-August and 2,841 on 21-August, so three sessions have retraced the prior weakness in full. Guinea-to-China freight has been running about $35-38/t against a delivered ore price of $70-74/t, meaning ocean freight is approaching HALF the delivered cost of the ore. A rising Capesize market into a widening contango is a delivered cost rising while the metal price falls, which compresses physical margin without appearing anywhere on a screen.

CARBON BORDER POLICY BECOMES A TRADE DISPUTE RATHER THAN A COMPLIANCE EXERCISE. CARRIED FORWARD AT MEDIUM/MEDIUM WITH AN UP TREND AND NO NEW DEVELOPMENT PUBLISHED SINCE, WHICH IS REPORTED AS SUCH RATHER THAN PADDED. BRICS environment and climate ministers formally objected on 22-August to the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, describing it as unilateral, punitive and discriminatory and warning of trade pressure on developing economies exporting aluminium into Europe. NO LEGAL CHANGE HAS OCCURRED - this is a ministerial statement, not an amendment. It is held at UP because the mechanism is already a price variable for European delivered metal and the dispute raises the probability of retaliation, carve-outs or delay. Aluminium is unusually exposed because carbon intensity varies by a factor of several between hydro-powered and coal-powered smelters, so any carbon border rule redraws trade routing rather than simply adding a uniform cost.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
